office.name: City of Westlake Permit Clerk
office.address: 1001 Bob Hardey Drive, P.O. Box 700, Westlake, LA 70669

facts.question: Do I need a permit to build a fence in Westlake?
facts.answer: Westlake's zoning ordinance defines a structure to include fences, and says no building or structure may be erected, altered, repaired or relocated until the building inspector issues a permit. Ask the permit clerk to confirm for your project.
facts.sourceTitle: Westlake Code of Ordinances § 12-2002 (definition of structure) and § 12-2008 (building permits) (Municode, updated through June 22, 2017)

facts.question: How do I apply?
facts.answer: Contact the city's permit clerk at 1001 Bob Hardey Drive, Westlake (337-433-0691).

facts.question: Where on the lot can a fence go?
facts.answer: The supplementary regulations printed in section 12-2006 of the zoning ordinance say fences may be put up along the boundaries of a lot or yard area, subject to the building code, and that one segment of a fence may be put up in a required side yard. A fence built near a street, public way or alley must not encroach on it; the owner of an encroaching fence can be required to remove it and pay for the survey.
facts.sourceTitle: Westlake Code of Ordinances § 12-2006 and § 5-1006 (Municode, updated through June 22, 2017)

facts.question: How tall can a fence be?
facts.answer: This isn't published online. Ask the Westlake permit clerk at 337-433-0691.

facts.question: Are there extra limits on a corner lot?
facts.answer: Yes. The supplementary yard regulations printed in section 12-2006 of the zoning ordinance say that on a corner lot in any district, nothing more than 3 feet tall (fence, wall, hedge, structure or planting) may be placed within the triangle formed by the two street lines and a line joining points 30 feet from their intersection.
facts.sourceTitle: Westlake Code of Ordinances § 12-2006 (supplementary regulations, yards) (Municode, updated through June 22, 2017)

facts.question: Does a swimming pool need a fence?
facts.answer: Pool barrier rules aren't printed in Westlake's code of ordinances; the building code it adopts may set them. Ask the Westlake permit clerk at 337-433-0691.
facts.sourceTitle: Westlake Code of Ordinances § 12-5031, Uniform Construction Code adopted (Municode, updated through June 22, 2017)

facts.question: Are any fence materials banned?
facts.answer: This isn't published online. Ask the Westlake permit clerk at 337-433-0691.

facts.question: Do I have to call Louisiana 811 before digging fence post holes?
facts.answer: Yes. Louisiana law says that before any excavation, the person digging must notify the regional notification center (Louisiana 811) at least 48 hours, but not more than 120 hours, before starting, not counting weekends and holidays. After notifying, you must wait at least 48 hours, counted from 7:00 a.m. on the next working day, before digging, unless Louisiana 811 tells you no utility operators need to be notified.
facts.sourceTitle: La. R.S. 40:1749.13, Excavation and demolition; prohibitions

facts.question: Does digging post holes by hand count?
facts.answer: Yes. The law defines excavation as moving or removing earth by powered, mechanical or manual means, and names digging and augering as examples. Manual probing is not counted as excavation.

facts.question: How do I contact Louisiana 811?
facts.answer: Call 811 or 1-800-272-3020, or submit a locate request online through Louisiana 811's website. Louisiana 811 says its service is free to anyone who disturbs the soil, whether with heavy equipment or hand tools.
